Durability Testing Lab

Long-term durability and aging tests simulating real-world usage conditions over extended periods.

Lab Overview

The HOLGENVY Durability Testing Lab is dedicated to predicting long-term product reliability through rigorous accelerated life testing. By subjecting products to intensified stress conditions — including extreme temperatures, humidity, vibration, and repeated mechanical cycling — we can simulate years of real-world usage within a matter of weeks. This approach enables our engineering teams to identify potential failure modes early in the development cycle, ensuring that every product bearing the HOLGENVY name delivers consistent performance over its intended lifespan.

Our lab operates around the clock, running continuous test sequences that replicate the most demanding job-site conditions. From power tools subjected to thousands of trigger pulls to batteries undergoing endless charge-discharge cycles, every critical component is pushed beyond normal operating parameters. The data collected from these tests feeds directly into our reliability engineering process, allowing us to refine designs, select superior materials, and validate product durability before market release.

Key Equipment

  • Continuous Run Test Stands (1000+ hour capability)
  • Temperature & Humidity Chambers (-40°C to +150°C)
  • Salt Spray Test Chamber
  • Vibration Test System
  • Drop Test Apparatus
  • Dust & Water Ingress (IP) Test Equipment

Testing Capabilities

  • Accelerated Life Testing (ALT)
  • Switch & Trigger Cycle Testing (100,000+ cycles)
  • Battery Charge/Discharge Cycle Testing
  • Environmental Stress Testing (temperature/humidity)
  • Corrosion & Salt Spray Resistance
  • IP Rating Verification (IPX4–IPX6)
  • Drop & Impact from Various Heights

Standards Covered

Our durability testing procedures comply with internationally recognized standards, including IEC 60068 for environmental testing, ASTM guidelines for accelerated aging methodologies, and GB/T 2423 for basic environmental test procedures. These standards provide a rigorous framework for evaluating product reliability under controlled conditions. In addition to standard compliance, our lab supports reliability prediction modeling and Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF) calculations, giving product teams quantitative data to validate design decisions and communicate expected product lifetimes to customers with confidence.

Testing Process

Every durability test at HOLGENVY follows a structured workflow designed to produce reliable, repeatable results. The process begins with sample setup and baseline measurement, where each test specimen is documented and its initial performance characteristics are recorded. This baseline serves as the reference point against which all subsequent measurements are compared, ensuring that any degradation or deviation is accurately quantified.

Once baselines are established, samples enter accelerated aging cycles tailored to the product type and intended use environment. During these cycles, periodic performance checks are conducted at predefined intervals to monitor gradual changes in functionality, power output, mechanical integrity, and safety parameters. If a failure occurs, the specimen is immediately removed for detailed failure analysis — including visual inspection, electrical diagnostics, and material examination — to determine the root cause.

The final deliverable is a comprehensive reliability report that documents all test conditions, performance trends, failure modes observed, and statistical analysis. This report includes calculated MTBF values and reliability predictions, providing product managers and engineers with the data needed to make informed decisions about design improvements, warranty policies, and production readiness.
